item.title: Icon Library - v1.6.3 [New App Release]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:

First public release.

Icon Library brings 3,879 Material Symbols icons into Splunk in three ways from one install:

  • Custom Dashboard Studio visualization (icon_library.icon_library) — Canvas-rendered tile with configurable color, size, background shape, glow, shadow, label, threshold-driven coloring and effects (icon swap / pulse / glow scale), hover tooltip, light/dark auto-theming, and click drilldown via Studio setToken. Requires Dashboard Studio 10.2 or newer.
  • Bundled SVG asset catalog — The same 3,879 icons as static SVGs at /static/app/icon_library/icons/<category>/<name>.svg. Use with splunk.image, asset slots, or CSS background-image. Works on all supported Splunk versions.
  • CSV lookup (icon_catalog) — | inputlookup icon_catalog exposes name, category, path, tags, popularity. Works on all supported Splunk versions.

Eight bundled dashboards demonstrate every feature (interactive README, four sample layouts, a service-health use case, the 256-icon showcase, and a searchable SVG browser).

Splunk Cloud–ready. Material Symbols font is base64-embedded — no external network requests. SVG catalog and lookup ship inside the app.


Short Description:
Custom Dashboard Studio visualization rendering 3,500+ Material Symbols icons with configurable appearance, threshold-driven coloring, labels, drilldown, and hover tooltips. Plus a bundled SVG catalog and CSV lookup. Embedded icon font — Splunk Cloud compatible.


Description:
The Icon Library app provides a custom visualization for Splunk Dashboard Studio that renders 3,879 Material Symbols icons directly on dashboards, with configurable color, size, background shape, shadow, glow, labels, alignment, rotation, threshold-driven coloring and effects, hover tooltips, and click drilldown. The icon font is base64-embedded in the visualization CSS to eliminate external network dependencies and ensure Splunk Cloud compatibility. The app also ships a bundled SVG asset catalog (the same 3,879 icons as static .svg files for use with splunk.image elements) and a CSV lookup (icon_catalog) for enumerating icons from SPL. Five bundled dashboards (README, Service Health Use Case, Icon Showcase, Icon Catalog Browser, SVG Reference) cover documentation, demos, and visual browsing.

item.title: TA Studio - v1.5.0 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:

New features

  • Dashboards page — bundle exported Simple XML / Dashboard Studio views; auto-added to add-on nav
  • Saved Searches & Reports page — manage savedsearches.conf with scheduling
  • Workflow Actions page — link and search drilldowns from result fields
  • Field Transforms page — delimited, multivalue, and reusable regex extractions
  • KV Store lookups — in addition to CSV lookups
  • Automatic lookups — apply a lookup to a source type at search time (LOOKUP-)
  • Field aliases (FIELDALIAS-) and calculated fields (EVAL-)
  • Search Macros page — manage parameterized macros.conf
  • Object tagging — full tags.conf manager (event types, hosts, sources, source types)
  • Raw .conf file editor — edit any conf under package/default/ verbatim, with AI assist
  • CIM compliance checker — scores a source type against every CIM data model
  • AI-generated app icons — flat SVG icons from a text description
  • xAI (Grok) added as an AI provider
  • AI input code is auto-tested and self-corrected (up to 2 fix attempts)
  • Cloud validation now runs SLIM packaging check


Short Description:
Build, import, validate, and package Splunk add-ons through a visual browser UI — no CLI. Create inputs (REST/shell/Python), alert actions, source types, field extractions, CIM mappings, lookups, and setup pages on the UCC Framework, run inputs and alerts in the browser to inspect their output, validate with AppInspect, and package for Splunkbase in one click.


Description:
TA Studio is a browser-based visual workbench for building Splunk® add-ons (TAs) on the Universal Configuration Console (UCC) Framework — without touching the command line. Authoring a quality add-on normally means working with the ucc-gen CLI, hand-editing globalConfig.json and a web of .conf files, and running AppInspect and packaging from a terminal. TA Studio replaces that workflow with a guided, point-and-click interface that runs entirely inside your own Splunk instance. From one UI you can create and manage data inputs (REST API, shell command, or Python modular inputs), alert actions (including Enterprise Security adaptive response), source types, field extractions with a live regex builder, CIM data model mappings, setup pages (accounts, proxy, logging), CSV lookups, and event types. You can import existing Splunk Add-on Builder and conf-based add-ons to modernize them, run inputs and alert actions right in the browser to inspect the events and output they produce, validate with AppInspect (including cloud checks) and review the results, then package a Splunkbase-ready archive in one click. TA Studio also includes built-in AI assistance to help you generate and refine input and alert-action code as you work. It otherwise runs entirely within your local Splunk environment: your add-on projects are not collected, transmitted, or stored outside your instance, and AI features send only the content you choose to submit to your selected AI provider.

item.title: AI Workbench (Adjutant AI) - v1.8.0 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:

Adjutant AI (formerly AI Workbench) — Release notes

What's new, improved, and fixed in each release, in plain language. This is the
customer-facing summary used for the Splunkbase release-notes section; the
full technical changelog lives in the project's detailed release notes.

Last updated: 2026-07-01

About version numbers. Releases once numbered 0.10–0.13 were renumbered to
1.0–1.3 to reflect production maturity — no behaviour changed. The current release is
1.8.0 (agent telemetry & OCSF export, content packs, all-tiers data-quality checks,
Splunk 10.x readiness, Dashboard Studio version-awareness). The 1.7.0 ServiceNow
integration and the 1.5.0 "Data Foundation & MCP OAuth" themes (data onboarding/quality
and OAuth 2.1 for MCP servers) are included below.

1.8.0 "Agent telemetry & OCSF export, content packs & all-tiers data quality"

New — your SOC can watch the agent (OCSF telemetry).

  • Adjutant AI emits its own activity as OCSF. Every LLM call, tool / MCP / ServiceNow call,
    configuration change, unattended run verdict, and policy refusal (the proof the controls
    actually fire) can be written as open-standard OCSF events to a Splunk index your Enterprise
    Security / SOC already watches — mapped to CIM via the community OCSF-CIM Add-On. Your SOC
    monitors our agent the same way it monitors everything else: on-prem, with no cloud egress.
  • You stay in control. It is off by default and Enterprise-gated. You provision and name
    the index     (the app ships no indexes.conf). Routing and content are resolved per Organisation
    / Business Unit    ; content export is denied by default and never exceeds your audit (DPIA) ceiling,
    with a server-side redaction check before anything is written.
  • See it immediately. A shipped admin dashboard — Adjutant AI — Behaviour (OCSF) — shows the
    token trend, model mix, tool/MCP egress with identity, the refusal and finding feeds, and a per-run
    drilldown, all on raw OCSF (no CIM Add-On required).

New — update Adjutant's content without waiting for a whole new app release.

  • Content packs. Almost everything Adjutant does well lives in its content — the
    skills, knowledge, and templates (playbooks). A content pack is a single, versioned
    file that lets us ship a corrected or improved content set straight to your install, and
    lets your admin apply it safely — no Splunkbase re-vetting cycle for a content fix.
  • Your changes are protected. Applying a pack upgrades only the items you haven't
    changed    . Anything your team has customised is left exactly as-is and clearly listed,
    never silently overwritten — and your Org/BU scoping is always preserved. After an
    import you get a per-item report, and the list of items that need manual reconciliation
    is downloadable as a CSV.
  • Safe by design. Every pack carries an integrity check, so a tampered or truncated
    file is refused. Imports live on the Backups page, which also shows which content
    version you're currently on — run a backup first and you can roll back in one click.
  • Retire without deleting. A pack can mark an item retired — it stays installed but
    is hidden and switched off everywhere (it can't be picked, run, or used by the
    assistant). An admin can re-enable it at any time by removing the tag.

Improved — data-quality checks for everyone, and Splunk 10.x readiness.

  • Data-quality ingestion checks are now available on every edition, including the free
    tier.     Checking whether a feed is actually landing and parsing correctly — on
    index=_internal, through TrackMe, and through Cribl Stream — is a baseline
    capability now, not a Professional add-on.
  • Ready for Splunk Enterprise 10.2 and 10.4. The app declares Python 3.9 and 3.13
    compatibility and has been audited against the 10.x platform changes (dashboards, the web
    framework, KV Store). Your admin still completes the standard KV Store engine migration as
    part of any 10.x upgrade.
  • Smarter Dashboard Studio building. The assistant now works from a single,
    version-aware map of what Dashboard Studio supports on your Splunk version — it won't
    reach for a chart type your version can't render, and when your Splunk is newer than what
    we've documented it builds conservatively and verifies the result.

Fixed.

  • Fewer false "the dashboard is blank" errors. A heavy Dashboard Studio dashboard that
    renders fine but slowly is no longer wrongly reported as blank — the assistant confirms the
    panels actually returned data before deciding, so it stops wasting a retry on a dashboard
    that was already correct. A genuinely blank dashboard is still caught.
  • TrackMe panels only when they belong. Fixed a rule that pushed a TrackMe feed-health
    panel onto every generated dashboard (and used a lookup that fails outside the TrackMe
    app). The assistant now adds a feed-health panel only when it's actually relevant, using a
    method that works in your app.

1.7.0 "ServiceNow integration" (included in the 1.8.0 release)

Renamed to Adjutant AI. The app is now Adjutant AI (formerly "AI Workbench").
This is a display-name change only — the in-app title (the easter egg now lives on
the dot of the "i" in Adjutant Ai), the app label, the documentation, and the
assistant's own self-description all say Adjutant AI. Nothing functional changed:
the Splunk app id, your saved searches/dashboards/models, KVStore data, and generated
artifact names are unchanged, so the upgrade is seamless.

New — run playbooks automatically, and from other Splunk apps.

  • On a schedule or on an event. A playbook can run unattended on a schedule
    (a "morning health check") or in response to a Splunk event — an alert, an ES
    correlation search, or an ITSI episode. When an event triggers it, the affected
    thing (the host, user, or entity in the alert) is handed to the playbook
    automatically, so it investigates exactly what fired. Two ready-made (disabled)
    examples are included to copy.
  • Adjutant AI as a building block for other apps. Other Splunk AI agents can now
    ask Adjutant AI to list and run your playbooks through a small, safe
    interface (an MCP server). Only playbooks you mark MCPready are exposed, every
    call must name the Org/BU it is for (which must be a business unit you have set up)
    as a safeguard, and runs go through the same governed, bounded service — never an
    open door. This interface is off by default — turn it on with one setting. When
    on, the tools can also appear inside Splunk's own MCP Server, reachable on the
    normal Splunk web address (no special port needed); you authenticate with a standard
    Splunk token. A ready-made, read-only example playbook ships enabled so there is
    always something to see the moment you switch the interface on.

New — "Report an issue" support packaging (all editions).

  • One click on any conversation (per-turn 🐞, the Ask panel, or the new Help tab)
    packages exactly what happened — versions, the resolved prompt, the tools and model used,
    the generated dashboards/searches, and every error and warning — into a single file.
  • Safe by construction: secrets are stripped before anything leaves the browser, and the
    file is encrypted to the support key, so it's safe to send over any channel.
  • It even tells you what kind of problem it looks like and matches known issues, so
    simple cases are solved without a back-and-forth.
  • Send it your way: download it and attach it to your own ticket, use the built-in
    support form, or email it. The Help tab (Report + Documentation + About) is always
    reachable — even if the app is locked by licensing.

New — ServiceNow, done properly (Professional + the servicenow feature). Read incidents,
changes, problems and the CMDB/CSDM in plain English — with bounded blast-radius / dependency
traversals ("what's the blast radius if this CI fails?"). Turn a Splunk alert, ITSI episode or ES
notable into a rich, deterministically rendered ServiceNow incident and write the number back to
the originating object (a re-fire updates, never duplicates; the closed-incident policy is
configurable). Security incidents (SIR) with MITRE ATT&CK, off until an admin enables them. Two
transports (REST or a ServiceNow MCP server), plus TISC threat-intel enrichment — all server-side
and allowlisted, so ServiceNow can never block the assistant. (Verified against the documented APIs
and unit-tested; final certification is on a live ServiceNow.)

New — run playbooks automatically, and from other apps. Playbooks can run unattended on a
schedule, or from a Splunk alert / ES correlation search / ITSI episode (the triggering entity is
handed to the run). Adjutant AI can also expose list / run over an inbound MCP server (off by
default, MCPready-only, Org/BU-scoped) — reachable inside Splunk's own MCP Server on the normal web
address, with a standard Splunk token.

New — "Report an issue" support packaging (all editions). One click packages a failing
conversation — secret-stripped and encrypted client-side — with an automatic problem
classification, plus an always-reachable Help tab even when the app is licence-locked.

New — Cribl Stream data-quality awareness (Professional+). Reads Cribl's own forwarded logs and
metrics to surface the timestamp / parse / dropped-event problems that happen inside Cribl, before
Splunk can see them — the "green in Splunk but timestamped wrong" blind spot — folded into one
readiness verdict. No Cribl Lake or Search required.

New — LLM reliability: retry, fallback & circuit breaker (Enterprise). A brief provider hiccup
(503 / 529 / rate-limit) auto-retries within a time budget; a per-config circuit breaker stops
hammering a provider that's down, then probes for recovery; and an ordered fallback transparently
switches to your next provider (and tells you which it used). Two new admin dashboards — LLM
Health and AI Activity — plus per-user / BU / org concurrency caps, all conservative and off
the critical path.

New — live model & cost catalogue (all editions). Models and prices come from a runtime catalogue
that updates without an app rebuild; automatic model discovery (Professional+) keeps it current
without ever logging your keys; an Enterprise admin screen adds price overrides and manual model
registration for private gateways.

Fixed. Generated Simple XML dashboards now share a single base search across panels (faster) and
get a top data-ingestion health panel; corrected a 3× Opus price over-charge (now server-side
authoritative, with Opus 4.8 and Fable 5 included).

1.5.0 "Data Foundation & MCP OAuth"

New

  • Connect to OAuth-protected MCP servers (OAuth 2.1). Adjutant AI can now
    connect to remote Model Context Protocol servers that require OAuth — including
    ServiceNow Action Fabric / MCP Server Console — using **authorization-code
  • PKCE for interactive connections and client-credentials / stored
    service-token for unattended ones. The Splunk backend is the OAuth client and
    token holder: the browser is used only for the login/consent redirect and never
    receives a token; tokens are stored encrypted in storage/passwords, refreshed
    automatically, and revoked on disconnect. Register an MCP server with
    Authentication type = OAuth 2.1, then click Connect. (Enterprise; rides
    the existing MCP feature gate — not separately licensed.)     See
    MCP_OAUTH.md.
  • Onboard new data sources, not just work with data already in Splunk.
    Describe a source — or attach a sample log file — and the assistant builds a
    deployment-ready set of Splunk add-ons (forwarder inputs, index-time
    parsing, search-time field extractions, CIM tags, and a deployment-server
    mapping) and hands you one downloadable package to push from your own
    deployment server. (Professional and up.)
  • "Is my data actually parsed correctly?" check. The assistant can tell you
    whether a sourcetype has ingestion or timestamp problems — events landing
    at the wrong time, truncated lines, broken line-breaking — by reading Splunk's
    own internal logs for you. It catches feeds that look healthy in TrackMe but
    are mis-onboarded. (Professional and up.)
  • Generated config is validated against your Splunk, and scored. Parsing
    configuration is checked against your instance's own configuration reference
    (no invented settings), and each source gets a 0–100 Data Quality Score
    with an A–F grade across the "Magic 8" onboarding best practices.
  • Attach a local sample file in Ask. Pick a log file from your computer and
    ask for the parsing config — even before the data is in Splunk. Only the file
    name is recorded in the audit trail, never the contents.

Improved

  • Works with the newest OpenAI "reasoning" models — including Azure AI
    Foundry GPT-5.4 / GPT-5.4-mini.     GPT-5-family and o-series models use a
    different request format for the output-length limit; the app now detects
    this automatically (and self-corrects if an Azure deployment has a custom
    name), so these models no longer fail on the first question. GPT-5.4 and
    GPT-5.4-mini appear in the OpenAI and Azure OpenAI model dropdowns. For
    Azure, the model field must match your deployment name, key-based
    authentication must be enabled, and the api-version must be 2025 or newer
    (the app's default now is).
  • More reliable generated dashboards. Help/explanation panels now render as
    formatted HTML instead of showing raw tags; dashboards no longer hit the
    "too many rows" error from an over-fine time-chart interval; CDTSM anomaly
    dashboards respect the model's 24-hour detection-window limit automatically;
    and the AI-Toolkit anomaly/forecast chart always renders as the proper
    visualization     (never falls back to a plain table).
  • Cleaner names for generated objects. Saved searches, models and dashboards
    the assistant creates now use an aiworkbench tag in their names instead of
    aiasst, to avoid confusion with Splunk's own "AI Assistant" app. Objects
    created earlier keep working unchanged.
  • Audit tab improvements. Adds a Business Unit column and a cascading
    Business Unit filter; the User filter is now a dropdown; you can filter
    by whether a request had an attachment; timestamps display in your local
    timezone    ; and the filters are tidied up. Token counts and the request outcome
    now record reliably (a fix to how audit completion events were written) — note
    that, per Splunk's permissions, capturing every user's activity requires the
    Organisation's audit index to be a normal (non-internal) index.

Earlier releases (1.0.0 – 1.4.3)

  • 1.4.3 — Clearer guidance and plain-language fixes when a free-tier LLM key hits its
    provider limits (e.g. Groq token-per-minute caps, Gemini zero-quota keys); the LLM config
    screen flags these up front.
  • 1.4.1 — Per-feature capability licensing with edition badges (Professional / Enterprise /
    MSP); gated features show a padlock, and nothing you created is ever deleted when a tier changes.
    Turn-level audit logging made reliable; more robust dashboard generation.
  • 1.4.0 — The assistant reads your own Splunk live (real search commands + installed
    visualizations) instead of guessing; Splunk Security Essentials detection content integrated.
  • 1.3.3 — TrackMe integration end-to-end (feed-health awareness + actions) with richer
    built-in platform knowledge.
  • 1.3.2 — First Splunkbase 1.x release: packaging and permissions hardening.
  • 1.3.1 — Fixed Org/BU edits dropping fields; safeguard to keep bundled templates correct
    after upgrades.
  • 1.3.0 — Real, per-Organisation audit logging of every AI interaction (Professional+).
  • 1.2.0 — Splunk Security Essentials content tools for templates.
  • 1.1.1 — Cisco Deep Time Series Model (CDTSM) templates: pre-trained anomaly detection and
    forecasting via the AI Toolkit, each with a proof dashboard.
  • 1.1.0 — Multi-tenancy and the Organisation / Business-Unit editor overhauled for clearer,
    safer tenant scoping.
  • 1.0.0 — The knowledge layer: ground answers in your organisation's own conventions.

(Releases before 1.0 are early pre-release history and are omitted here.)

Known issues

  • Open the assistant from inside another app. Adjutant AI is a "host shell":
    reach it from a navigation-menu entry inside Search, Enterprise Security, ITSI,
    or your own apps — not by clicking the app tile directly. Everything it creates
    lands in the namespace of the app you opened it from.
  • Some Data Foundation features need self-hosted Splunk. The
    configuration-reference grounding and config-package generation (1.5.0) read
    files on the Splunk server, so they are unavailable on Splunk Cloud; the
    assistant says so and continues with what it can.

When a published fix resolves a tracked GitHub issue, it is summarised here with
its issue number — for example: "Fixed: a dashboard panel could display raw HTML
markup as text instead of formatting it (#123)."


Short Description:
A workbench for Splunk, not just a chatbot. Analyse, correlate and build across SPL, dashboards, alerts, AI Toolkit / MLTK, ES, ITSI and TrackMe through tools that understand each one — plus any MCP server you add. Pick your LLM: Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure, Groq, Gemini, Bedrock, Ollama, OpenRouter. Multi-tenant, multi-tier (Free, Pro, Enterprise, MSP).


Description:
Adjutant AI is a generative workspace for Splunk. Not a chatbot bolted onto search, but a real workbench where you investigate, analyse and build with tools that understand Splunk. It is a host shell with no use cases of its own. Everything derives from the Splunk app a user opens it from and their roles. Install once on the Search Head, then embed it in the apps your users already live in: Search, ITSI, Enterprise Security, your SOC and MSP customer apps. The same engine renders a different experience per app and writes into that app's namespace. Users never leave the app they came from. Ask in plain English. Get back validated SPL, Simple XML and Dashboard Studio dashboards, alerts, lookups, reports and MLTK machine-learning pipelines, grounded in your running Splunk (your knowledge objects, live command syntax, CIM models), run for real before they are saved as normal knowledge objects owned by the calling user. The depth is the difference. Where an MCP-only assistant talks through one broad door, Adjutant AI ships fine-grained, Splunk-aware tools across Core, Enterprise Security, ITSI, TrackMe, ServiceNow and the AI Toolkit, each scoped to one job and run under your existing Splunk ACLs. Extend it with HTTP tools or any MCP server. New in 1.8.0: your SOC can watch the agent. Adjutant AI emits its own activity (LLM calls, tool and ServiceNow calls, config changes, unattended run verdicts and policy refusals) as open-standard OCSF events to an index Enterprise Security already watches, mapped to CIM. On-prem, no cloud egress, off by default, with a Behaviour dashboard. Control is the product; now it is observable. Also included: ServiceNow integration (read incidents, changes and the CMDB; turn an alert, ITSI episode or ES notable into a ServiceNow or SIR incident with the number written back), governed unattended playbooks, and a Data Foundation add-on builder. Bring your own LLM: Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Groq, Google Gemini, AWS Bedrock, Ollama (local, fully offline) or OpenRouter. Keys stay server-side. Organisations and Business Units resolve from the calling app and roles. Editions. Personal is free: no license key, no registration, no trial clock. One user gets the full core engine: SPL generation, dashboards, alerts, machine learning, the knowledge layer and bring your own LLM. Genuinely free, not a demo. Professional adds unlimited users, three Business Units, session History, Tokens and Costs, and ES, ITSI and TrackMe awareness. Enterprise adds the security workflows (ES notable triage, user, host and IOC investigation, lateral movement detection, phishing triage, ITSI root cause analysis), the audit trail with governance logging, LLM fallback and unlimited Business Units. item.title: Splunk Add-on for CyberArk EPM - v5.0.0 [Version Update]

Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:

  • Removed deprecated inputs: Application Events, Policy Audit, and Threat Detection. Replaced by Inbox Events and Policy Audit Events inputs with API Type: Aggregated Events.
  • Dropped Python 3.7 and 3.8 support. Minimum required Python version is now 3.9. Added Python 3.13 support (supported range: 3.9–3.13).

Description:
The Splunk Add-on for CyberArk EPM allows a Splunk software administrator to pull aggregated events of Application Events, Policy Audit, and Threat Detection categories using the cloud administration APIs of CyberArk EPM. Moreover, it can also collect the logs related to Policies, Computers, and Computer Groups. This add-on provides modular inputs and CIM-compatible knowledge to use with other Splunk apps, such as Splunk Enterprise Security. This add-on is only Python3 compatible.

item.title: Log Continuity Manager for Splunk - v1.0.0 [New App Release]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:

## Version 1.0.0

Initial public release of Log Continuity Manager for Splunk.

### Included in this release

- Log continuity health dashboard

- Current violations view

- Monitoring targets view

- Manage targets workflow

- Discovery workflow for candidate monitoring targets

- Monitoring coverage gaps view

- Quick Add Target workflow

- Recovery history tracking

- Lookup-backed monitoring status model

- Redundancy-aware interruption handling

- Target update and operational management functions

### Purpose

This release provides an operational workflow for monitoring expected log continuity, identifying interrupted targets, discovering untracked sources, and tracking recovery events in Splunk environments.


Short Description:
A Splunk app for monitoring log continuity, detecting interruptions, managing monitoring targets, tracking recoveries, and improving visibility into ingestion health.


Description:
Log Continuity Manager for Splunk helps security and operations teams monitor whether expected log sources continue sending data on time. It provides a practical workflow to define monitoring targets, detect log interruptions, identify untracked sources, manage monitored targets, and review recovery history from a single app. The app is designed for teams that need visibility into log continuity health without building custom searches and dashboards from scratch. It supports target-based monitoring using host, index, source, and sourcetype combinations, and helps reduce false positives in redundant environments through redundancy-aware interruption handling. With its operational views, users can discover live data sources, compare discovered sources against configured monitoring targets, add new targets quickly, manage target settings, review current interruptions, and track when interrupted sources recover. This makes it easier to maintain monitoring coverage, reduce blind spots, and improve confidence in Splunk data ingestion health.

item.title: Local AI Assistant for Splunk - v1.0.2 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:

Changes in This Release

  • Reworked configuration page.
  • Added Key for Ollama instances behind Reverse Proxy with Bearer Token authentication.
  • Resolved several minor compatibility and stability issues.


Short Description:
Run local LLM prompts against your Splunk data — no API keys, no cloud, complete data privacy.


Description:
OAI (Observalytics AI) integrates your local Ollama instance directly into Splunk, enabling AI-powered analysis without sending data to external services. The Problem: Security and operations teams want AI-driven insights but face compliance, privacy, and cost concerns with cloud-based AI APIs. Splunk AI Assistant timeout setting

Added a new Guardrails setting, Splunk AI Assistant timeout, which controls the maximum number of seconds before a Splunk AI Assistant tool call times out.

Improved configuration specification coverage

Added entries to mcp.conf.spec for eight previously undocumented \[server] configuration keys that were causing btool validation errors.

When a user does not have the mcp\_tool\_admin capability, the app now displays a specific error message instead of a generic fallback error: "You do not have the mcp\_tool\_admin capability required to manage tools."

**Notes / Considerations**

- Guardrails settings can now be updated from the MCP app UI without restarting splunkd.

- The Splunk AI Assistant timeout setting applies to Splunk AI Assistant tool calls and controls the maximum time allowed before a call times out.

- Administrators who previously managed MCP server limits and rate controls through configuration should review the new Guardrails section on the MCP landing page.

  • Workload — a redesigned Versioning experience. The Versioning metadata tab is rebuilt as a structured, filterable version history: each tracked change is shown as an expandable card with who changed it, when, and what changed, and a colour-coded before/after diff for every affected property — the search itself, but also non-search settings such as the schedule and time range.   • Full control over your Virtual Tenants landing page. TrackMe users can now organise the Virtual Tenants overview exactly the way they work — drag tenant cards, Virtual Group categories, and the groups within each category into any order (saved globally for all users), and the Administration menu is grouped into clear labelled sections.   • Replica trackers & tenants — a major reliability pass. Replicated entities are no longer re-evaluated locally (which could corrupt their state and cause them to disagree with the source); they now mirror the source state, their table display fields and status are restored, Tenant Home counters refresh immediately after a replica run, and the Manage/Execute replica screens are repaired with clear replica-context messaging.

  • More helpful alerts & AI. Stateful-alert notifications now embed Workload error traces, disruption-grace states are labelled correctly, the AI status report stays informational (no un-actionable advisor prompts in one-way emails), and Claude Sonnet 5 is suggested as the default Anthropic model.

item.title: TheHive/Cortex - v4.2.0 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:

# Release Notes

## Summary

Version 4.2.0 is a **stability and reliability release**. It hardens the alert actions and adaptive responses (alert/case creation), fixes several observable parsing edge cases that could silently drop data or get the whole payload rejected by TheHive, and corrects date/timestamp handling in TTP processing and the Cases LIST search command. No new feature is introduced and no configuration change is required — this is a safe, drop-in update from v4.1.0.

## Improvements & Bug Fixes

### 🧩 Alert Actions: robust observable parsing

- **Valid observable sub-field types**: observable sub-fields are now read with

their documented `snake_case` names (`\:is_ioc`, `\:sighted`,

`\:sighted_at`, `\:ignore_similarity`) and coerced to the native

types TheHive expects. Previously the boolean `sighted` value was forwarded as

the raw string `"1"`, causing TheHive to reject the request with

`BadRequest - Invalid json` and silently dropping `is_ioc`, `sighted_at` and

`ignore_similarity`. The sighting timestamp now also accepts float epoch

values and is normalized to milliseconds.

- **Multi-value observable splitting**: fixed a regex that split observable

values on the literal letter `n` instead of a newline, which mangled

multi-value observables.

- **Resilient row handling**: improved handling of sanitized rows to avoid

`KeyError` exceptions on incomplete events, and corrected the `sourceRef`

variable used in debug logging.

### 📎 Alert Actions: reliable result attachments

- Result attachments (`attach_results`) now use a **uniquely-named temporary

directory per invocation** instead of a fixed file name in the shared system

temp directory. On Windows (where `splunkd` runs as the SYSTEM service and the

temp directory is `C:\WINDOWS\TEMP`), the previous behavior caused concurrent

or overlapping runs to collide on the same path, raising

`Permission denied` / `No such file or directory` and **preventing the second

alert/case of a multi-result search from being created** (e.g. UC2 — "Saved

search, several alerts"). Temp files are now always cleaned up, and the

attachment result is guarded against `None`.

### ⏱️ TTP & timestamp handling

- `_time` is now parsed as a **float** when processing TTPs, preventing failures

on sub-second timestamps.

- When the configured `timestamp_field` is missing from an event, processing now

**falls back to the current time** instead of failing.

### 🔎 Search commands

- **Cases LIST respects Date settings (#126)**: the Cases LIST action now

correctly applies the configured date range instead of ignoring it.

## Deployment Notes

- **Prerequisite**: Python 3.9 (matches Splunk's bundled interpreter).

- **Migration Path**:

- **From v4.1.0 / v4.0.0**: non-breaking update. Existing configuration,

accounts, instances and certificates are preserved.

- **From v3.9.0 (Direct Upgrade)**: you can upgrade directly to v4.2.0.

- **⚠️ CRITICAL**: if upgrading from v3.x, the

**[v4.0.0 migration instructions](./v4.0.0.md) are mandatory** and remain

valid for this version (UCC architecture migration, breaking configuration

changes, and new credential storage). Please read them carefully before

proceeding.

- **Upgrade tip (Windows / on-prem)**: never delete the app's `local/` folder.

Stop Splunk, back up `local/`, deploy the new build, restore `local/`, then

start Splunk.


Description:
This TA allows to add interaction features between TheHive or Cortex (https://www.strangebee.com/) and Splunk. It allows to retrieve all kind of information from TheHive/Cortex and to perform actions on these instances using Splunk, from a search or from a predefined dashboard. This TA is supporting only TheHive 5. For having an app supporting TheHive 3 or 4, please check the oldest releases. It's also supporting the Cortex 3 version. More information here: https://github.com/LetMeR00t/TA-thehive-cortex

日本語の半角の文字列を全角にするコマンド han2zen コマンドと全角の文字列を半角にする zen2han コマンドを提供します。

  • 明示的に指定しており、Python 3.13 をオプトインした環境でも本コマンドは 3.9 で実行されます。
  • Splunk が将来 Python 3.9 のサポートを終了した後は、純 Python 版の 2.0.0 系を利用してください。

item.title: Data Heartbeat - v1.4.1 [New App Release]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:

A security, reliability, and Cloud-readiness hardening release. Validated with Splunk AppInspect (cloud + future) and live-tested on a single Splunk 10.2 instance and a 3-member Search Head Cluster.

Security

  • Alert target secrets (Slack/Teams/webhook URLs, email recipient lists) are now isolated in admin-read-only KV-store collections. Non-admins keep a read-only Monitor view but can no longer read configured webhook/recipient values via the KV REST API, the audit log, the backup copy, or scheduled-alert results.
  • The custom REST endpoint is capability-gated: enable/disable monitoring requires edit_search_scheduler or admin_all_objects; Send Test Alert requires admin_all_objects.
  • Outbound alert delivery includes SSRF protection — internal/loopback/link-local/private/cloud-metadata (incl. RFC 6598 CGNAT and IPv4-mapped IPv6) targets are blocked.
  • Uninstall instructions now scrub all seven KV-store collections (where secrets persist) before the app is removed.

Reliability & data integrity

  • Splunk Cloud / 10.2 compatibility: python.required = 3.9, 3.13 so the alert action and admin endpoint run on the platform default (3.9) everywhere and prefer 3.13 where enabled.
  • Detection now uses tstats (keyed on index time) instead of | metadata — no 10,000-sourcetype cap, robust to clock skew; empty/garbage thresholds still flag.
  • Settings, alert config, audit history, and metrics live in KV-store and replicate across a Search Head Cluster, and survive app upgrades. Per-row edits use single-key upserts to avoid lost updates.
  • Consolidated alert digests: one notification per destination per fire (not one per flagged source). Alert bodies show the real "last event" age.
  • Upgrades migrate prior CSV-based data into KV without overwriting your settings; Backup/Restore is guarded so an empty source can't destroy the recovery point.

Accessibility & UX

  • Full keyboard operation and ARIA labelling for the Monitor table — importance/notes/alert-action editors, the importance picker, threshold inputs, filter chips, and modal controls.
  • Non-admins get a coherent read-only experience (write controls hidden/inert; clear messaging).
  • Add-Sourcetype picker is capped for large environments; clearer onboarding and discovery labelling.

Documentation

  • README corrected for the seven KV-store collections, the admin-only secret model, tstats -based detection, the consolidated-digest model, and a correct uninstall procedure.

Upgrade note

Existing CSV-based settings/audit/metrics migrate to KV-store automatically on first dashboard load after upgrade. No manual steps required.


Short Description:
Know the moment a data source goes silent. Data Heartbeat monitors every source type in your Splunk environment and fires Slack, Teams, webhook, or email alerts the instant data stops flowing — before gaps turn into blind spots.


Description:
Data Heartbeat monitors your Splunk environment for source types that have stopped sending data. When a data source goes silent — whether from a misconfigured forwarder, a failed log shipper, or a broken integration — Data Heartbeat detects the gap and alerts you before the silence becomes a blind spot. Every monitored source type has a configurable threshold, measured in minutes. When no data arrives within that window, the app flags the source type and fires your chosen alert action: Slack, Microsoft Teams, a generic webhook, or email via Splunk's built-in SMTP relay. Key features: • Monitor dashboard — a live status table showing every tracked source type, the minutes since its last event, its threshold, and its importance level, with color-coded severity (green, yellow, red, and critical). • Per-row alert actions — each source type can use its own notification target, independent of the global default. • Auto Discovery — a nightly scan that surfaces new source types appearing in your environment and queues them for review. • Importance tagging — mark business-critical sources as High, Medium, or Low importance. When a high-importance source goes silent, the app raises a red-alert banner. • Settings page — configure global defaults (threshold, alert action, and notification target), enable or disable the monitoring pipeline, and test alert actions without waiting for a real outage. • Audit log — a full history of every configuration change, with timestamps and user attribution. • No index footprint — all configuration is stored in KV Store, so no custom indexes are required. Data Heartbeat is compatible with Splunk Enterprise 8.2+, Splunk Cloud Classic, and Splunk Cloud Victoria.
